info.title: Your RQTH orientation, before entering the working world
info.lead: HandiDiag is for students of the school preparing to work: it helps you see whether official recognition (RQTH) could make sense for your career plan, and who to talk to.
info.what: The RQTH (recognition of the status of disabled worker, in France) is an administrative decision. It can give access to measures for finding or keeping a job, such as workplace or schedule adjustments and financial support. It concerns people whose ability to get or keep a job is reduced by a lasting impairment of physical, sensory, mental or psychological functions. The application is personal and voluntary.
info.what_falc: The RQTH is a decision made by the French administration. It can help you find a job or keep it. For example: adapted hours, an adapted workstation, money for equipment. The application is personal. Nobody can make it for you.
does: It explains the process in plain words.

It first asks whether the school's disability office follows you. If yes, it moves on to the RQTH questions. If not, it offers to see (a few questions) whether the office could be useful, then lets you choose: continue with the RQTH or stop here.
It tells you whether it may be useful to talk to someone, and who: the disability office for your studies, the Career Center for the working world.
It gives you a kit to move forward, plus resources at school, nationally and in law.
does_falc: It explains the process in plain words.
It first asks whether the disability office follows you. If yes, it asks RQTH questions. If not, it offers to see whether the office can help. Then you choose: continue or stop.
It says whether it may be useful to talk to someone, and who.
It gives official links, contacts and a to-do list.
not: It never says whether you will be granted recognition: only the MDPH decides.
It does not replace a doctor, the MDPH or an adviser.
It sends your answers to nobody.
not_falc: It does not make a diagnosis.
It does not say if you will get the RQTH. The MDPH decides.
It does not replace a doctor or an adviser.
It sends your answers to nobody.
privacy: No account, no email address requested.
Your answers stay in your browser. They disappear when you reload or close the page.
Only anonymous counters (for example: number of completed questionnaires) may be sent. You can refuse below.
No cookie, no tracker, no third-party service.
privacy_falc: Your answers stay on your device. They are erased when you close the page.
We only count how many people finished. We do not know who. You can say no below.
info.stats_label: I agree to contribute to anonymous statistics (aggregated counters, not linked to my detailed answers).
info.start_hint: Between 8 and 13 questions, about 6 minutes. Any question can be skipped with « I prefer not to answer ».
info.kit_link: Go straight to the resource kit

path.text: See whether the disability office could be useful, then, if you wish, answer about ten RQTH questions, no medical detail.

path.text: Prepare the process with the kit and the resources.

info.calm_title: Disability, RQTH: words that sometimes feel scary
calm: Many students are concerned. Most situations supported at school are invisible disabilities: “dys” disorders, disabling illnesses, psychological or attention difficulties.
Asking for an accommodation is not asking for a favour: it gives everyone the same conditions to succeed.
Finding out commits you to nothing. You stay free to continue or not, at your own pace.
The RQTH is a personal and voluntary step. You stay free to talk about it to an employer or not.
At the disability office, only the information useful for the accommodation is shared.
info.pole_title: And at school? The disability office
info.pole_text: The disability office meets you for a first interview: building trust, respecting your privacy, identifying your needs, explaining the rules. It then sets up the accommodations, follows you throughout your studies and helps with entering the working world.
info.pole_link: See resources at school, nationally and in law

kit.title: Resource kit
kit.intro: Everything you need to move forward, with official sources. Always check forms and the list of documents on the official websites: they can change.
kit.checklist_intro: Tick items as you go. Nothing is saved: if you reload the page, the list is emptied.
checklist: Read the official page about the RQTH
Find the MDPH for my département
Note my difficulties and their effects on my studies or work
Book an appointment with a doctor for the medical certificate
Fill in the application form, including the “life project” section
Gather the requested documents (official list): ID, proof of address, useful medical documents
Submit the file (online or by post) and keep a copy
Note the submission date and watch for the reply letter

guide.title: Find out more
guide.text: Read the official page and the summary on this page. You do not have to decide anything at this stage.

guide.title: Talk to someone you trust
guide.text: A disability officer, an occupational or prevention physician, an adviser: your orientation list suggests starting points.

guide.title: See a doctor
guide.text: A doctor fills in a medical certificate describing the effects of your health situation. You can bring it with your file.

guide.title: Prepare the file
guide.text: Fill in the MDPH application form and gather the requested documents. Do not hesitate to ask the MDPH or an adviser for help.

guide.title: Submit the application
guide.text: The application goes to the MDPH of your département, online or by post. Keep a copy of everything you send.

guide.title: Wait for the decision
guide.text: The CDAPH commission decides. Waiting times vary by area (département). Once you receive the decision, you choose who you tell.

vigilance: HandiDiag does not replace a doctor, the MDPH or an adviser.
Always check forms and the list of documents on the official websites.
Keep the original of your decision notice.
Do not share medical information through insecure channels.

resources.title: Resources
resources.lead: Reliable contacts and texts: at school, nationally and in law.
resources.efrei_intro: At school, several people can listen to you. Write to them by e-mail: you choose what you share.
resources.steps_title: How the disability office supports you

steps.title: First interview
steps.text: Building trust, respecting privacy, identifying needs, explaining the rules and the documents needed.

steps.title: Setting up accommodations
steps.text: The office uses internal tools to track accommodations.

steps.title: Talking with teaching teams
steps.text: If needed, depending on the disability: passing on instructions, practical situations, explanations.

steps.title: Follow-up throughout your studies
steps.text: The office checks that accommodations match your needs and attends exam boards if needed.

steps.title: Help entering the working world
steps.text: Partner companies are looking for graduates with disabilities.

resources.freq_title: The most common accommodations at school
resources.freq_intro: Separate rooms and extra time are the most common. Digital tools and specialised equipment play a growing role.
resources.types_text: Most supported situations are invisible disabilities: “dys” disorders (reading, writing, language) and disabling illnesses come first, followed by psychological, cognitive and motor difficulties, autism, and hearing or vision impairments. Each situation gets an individual response.
school: Several departments contribute to accessibility: information systems, transformation, student life, teaching innovation, cross-cutting projects and a research lab.
Many staff members have been trained in Mental Health First Aid (PSSM).
Accessibility and inclusion are a responsibility shared by the whole community, not just the disability service.
resources.source_pole: Source: information sheet from Efrei's disability office.
resources.national_intro: These organisations and associations are independent from the school. They can inform, support or defend your rights.
resources.assoc_intro: Chosen for the most common situations at school and for young people in education or job hunting.
resources.assoc_more: More associations: the ONISEP directory (in French)
resources.law_intro: A few simple landmarks from national texts. This is general information, not legal advice: each school or employer applies them through its own procedures, and you should always check the up-to-date texts.
